verdicts.trueWording: we had received 700 legitimate submissions and 500 machine-written ones
verdicts.note: Raw NPR page (curl, 200, datePublished 2023-02-24, All Things Considered). Quote appears word for word attributed to Neil Clarke: "By the time we closed on the 20th, around noon, we had received 700 legitimate submissions and 500 machine-written ones," he said. Every limb (Clarke; NPR; at the point submissions closed; 700/500) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Without a concerted effort to break the systems out of their default register
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page (curl, 200). Full sentence: "Without a concerted effort to break the systems out of their default register, the text they spit out is, while grammatically and semantically sound, ineffably generated," preceded by "you'll have noticed a certain quality to the responses generated." Both limbs (generated quality; default register breakable by concerted effort) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: half a percent of all articles on PubMed contain "delve"
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page. "When half a percent of all articles on research site PubMed contain the word 'delve' - 10 to 100 times more than did a few years ago - it's hard to conclude anything other than an awful lot of medical researchers using the technology..." Both the half-percent figure and the 10-to-100x comparison are on the page (in the Jeremy Nguyen passage).

verdicts.trueWording: "Explore", "tapestry", "testament" and "leverage" all appear far more frequently
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page, paragraph beginning "According to another dataset": the four words "all appear far more frequently in the system's output than they do in the internet at large." All four words and the comparison limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: In Nigeria, "delve" is much more frequently used in business English
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page: "In Nigeria, 'delve' is much more frequently used in business English than it is in England or the US." Claim's "English or American English" maps to the page's "England or the US"; substance identical.

verdicts.trueWording: If AI-ese sounds like African English, then African English sounds like AI-ese
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page, paragraph beginning "And that's the final indignity." The warning limb is carried by the surrounding text ("Calling people a 'bot' is already a schoolyard insult... how much worse will it get when a significant chunk of humanity sounds like the AI systems they were paid to train?"), and the article's frame throughout is AI-ese as a tell.

verdicts.trueWording: fawning obsequiousness... hammered into line through reinforcement learning with human feedback
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page, paragraph beginning "Some of the tells are obvious": "The fawning obsequiousness of a wild language model hammered into line through reinforcement learning with human feedback marks chatbots out." Attribution of the obsequiousness to RLHF is explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: Handcrafted: artwork made by an artist without AI-generation programs
verdicts.note: Live help.drivethrurpg.com returned Cloudflare 403 ("Just a moment..."); recovered via Wayback raw capture https://web.archive.org/web/20251005160536id_/... (200), page dated October 28, 2024. Under "What do the different filters mean?": "Handcrafted -> Artwork was made by an artist practicing their craft, without the use of AI-generation programs." The definition mentions artwork only - no writing clause - so the "purely in terms of artwork" limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: starting on July 31, content made "primarily" of AI-generated writing not allowed
verdicts.note: Raw EN World thread page (curl, 200), opening post by Whizbang Dustyboots dated Jul 25, 2023, block quotation attributed to Gizmodo: "another update states that starting on July 31, any content that is made of 'primarily' of AI-generated writing will not be allowed." The preceding sentence in the same quotation names "the DriveThru Marketplaces (which includes Dungeon Masters Guild)" as the policies' subject; the Jul 25 2023 thread date fixes the year.

verdicts.trueWording: "We acknowledge enforcement challenges... trust in the goodwill of our partners"
verdicts.note: Raw EN World page, same Gizmodo block quotation: "'We acknowledge enforcement challenges,' says the policy page on both DMsGuild and Roll20, 'and trust in the goodwill of our partners to offer customers unique works based primarily on human creativity'." Both substantive limbs verbatim. On attribution the page names the policy pages as DMsGuild's and Roll20's, and separately identifies Dungeon Masters Guild as "a subsidiary of OneBookShelf" that "officially announced a policy change" - so "the OneBookShelf policy" is supported through that chain rather than by that phrase appearing on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: participants performed below chance levels in identifying AI-generated poems
verdicts.note: Raw nature.com article page (curl, 200). Abstract: "We conducted two experiments with non-expert poetry readers and found that participants performed below chance levels in identifying AI-generated poems (46.6% accuracy...)." Non-expert-reader limb supported by the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: Observed accuracy was in fact slightly lower than chance (46.6%
verdicts.note: Raw nature.com page, Results / "Study 1: distinguishing AI-generated from human-written poems": "Observed accuracy was in fact slightly lower than chance (46.6%, chi-sq (1, N = 16340) = 75.13, p < 0.0001)." Figure and study location both as claimed.

verdicts.trueWording: more likely to judge AI-generated poems as human-authored than actual human-authored poems
verdicts.note: Raw nature.com page, Abstract: "Notably, participants were more likely to judge AI-generated poems as human-authored than actual human-authored poems (chi-sq (2, N = 16,340) = 247.04, p < 0.0001)." Quote verbatim; both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: The largest effect is on "rhythm"... much better rhythm than famous poets' poems
verdicts.note: Raw nature.com page, Study 2 results: "The largest effect is on 'rhythm': AI-generated poems are rated as having much better rhythm than the poems written by famous poets (Welch's t (6694.647) = 35.319, p < 0.0001, Cohen's d = 0.847)." Both the largest-effect limb and the rhythm comparison are explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: all 5 AI-generated poems are rated more highly in overall quality
verdicts.note: Raw nature.com page, Study 2, sentence citing Fig. 2: "This is remarkably consistent; as seen in Fig. 2, all 5 AI-generated poems are rated more highly in overall quality than all 5 human-authored poems." Study 2's design (5 real and 5 AI-generated poems per poet, rated on overall quality) is stated in the same section.
